raw_case_text:
A 73-year-old man was referred from a private practitioner to Govt. Dental College, Calicut with ulcers in his oral cavity, fever, chest pain and cough since 2 weeks and he also noticed skin lesions over face and forearm.
Oral examination revealed ulcerated and necrotic lesions located on the labial mucosa, lateral borders of tongue, hard and soft palate [Figures 1a and b]. The lesions were covered by a pseudomembrane and were extremely painful to palpation. Bilateral submandibular lymphadenopathy was noted. Extraoral examination revealed multiple nodular lesions on the chin, right side of the face and upper lip with an erythematous surface [Figure 1c]. Hair loss was noticed on the chin, upper lip and the eyebrows. Multiple plaques were seen on the ventral surface of the forearm and dorsal aspect of thigh [Figures 1d and e]. They were pale in color compared to the surrounding skin and there was a rise in local temperature. A firm consistency was felt while palpating these lesions.
The patient had malaise and fatigue at the time of examination, with a body temperature of 38.2 C, pulse rate of 82/min, respiratory rate of 18 cycles/min and blood pressure of 140/86 mm/Hg. Routine blood investigation showed a hemoglobin level of 9.4 g/dl, 7800 leucocytes (60% neutrophils, 36% lymphocytes and 4% eosinophils) and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (24 mm/h). Acid fast bacillus (AFB) examination of sputum did not reveal any acid fast bacilli (Zeihl Neelson stain)
An incisional biopsy of the labial mucosa showed the presence of epithelioid cell granulomas in the connective tissue with numerous histiocytes, many of which formed multinucleated giant cells. The cytoplasm of the histiocytes showed the presence of small round to oval basophilic bodies surrounded by a clear halo, which is the characteristic feature of histoplasma capsulatum [Figures 2a-c]. These organisms stained highly positive with Gomori's Methanimine Silver stain [Figures 3a and b]. The patient was found to be HIV negative (comb and tridot tests).
Antifungal therapy was started with intravenous liposomal amphotericin B at 0.7 mg/kg/day administered for 10 days which was replaced by oral itraconazole 200 mg BD for 6 months. Patient's respiratory symptoms showed marked improvement after 3 days of medication. The oral and cutaneous lesions resolved after 2 months. Patient is under regular follow up and was free of symptoms at the end of 1 year.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 73-year-old man presented with a 2-week history of painful oral ulcers, fever, chest pain, cough, and skin lesions over the face and forearm.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was referred by a private practitioner to a dental college in Calicut, India, after developing painful oral cavity ulcers, fever, chest pain, cough, malaise, fatigue, and nodular/plaque skin lesions over his face, forearm, and thigh over 2 weeks.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for oral ulcers, fever, chest pain, cough, malaise, fatigue, skin lesions, and localized facial hair loss.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: temperature 38.2 C, HR 82/min, RR 18/min, BP 140/86 mmHg. Intraoral exam: extremely painful, pseudomembrane-covered ulcerated and necrotic lesions on the labial mucosa, lateral borders of the tongue, and hard and soft palate. Lymphatics: bilateral submandibular lymphadenopathy. Cutaneous exam: multiple erythematous nodular lesions on the chin, right face, and upper lip with localized hair loss over the chin, upper lip, and eyebrows, plus firm, pale, warm plaques on the ventral forearm and dorsal thigh.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs: Hb 9.4 g/dL, WBC 7,800/mm3 (60% neutrophils, 36% lymphocytes, 4% eosinophils), ESR 24 mm/h; HIV negative (Comb and Tridot tests); sputum Ziehl-Neelsen stain negative for acid-fast bacilli.
objective.advanced_workup: Incisional biopsy of labial mucosa: epithelioid cell granulomas in connective tissue with numerous histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells containing small round-to-oval basophilic bodies surrounded by a clear halo, strongly positive on Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stain.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated mucocutaneous and pulmonary histoplasmosis in an HIV-negative patient. Confirmation: Labial mucosal biopsy histopathology and GMS staining demonstrating characteristic intracellular Histoplasma capsulatum yeast forms within histiocytes. Plan & clinical course: Treated with IV liposomal amphotericin B (0.7 mg/kg/day for 10 days) followed by oral itraconazole (200 mg BID for 6 months). Respiratory symptoms improved within 3 days, oral and cutaneous lesions resolved after 2 months, and the patient remained symptom-free at 1-year follow-up.
